articles.title: A strong emotional bond with a mother predicts resilience after childhood trauma
articles.summary: A large study reveals that adolescents who experience a warm relationship with a mother figure and limit their sedentary screen time are more likely to demonstrate resilience in adulthood following childhood abuse.

articles.title: Men and women report similar levels of “duty sex,” and similar reasons behind it
articles.summary: Sex out of obligation is often treated as a red flag in relationships. But a new study suggests it may serve a purpose for some people, appearing most often when they sense their relationship could be under threat.

articles.title: Horror isn’t just intense fear, new psychology study suggests
articles.summary: Fear tends to involve possible danger ahead, while horror often follows learning about something that shouldn’t happen. A new study suggests that graphic, extreme descriptions of harm push readers toward horror by making events feel abnormal.

articles.title: Low-dose aspirin linked to 70% lower dementia risk, but there's a catch
articles.summary: A common, inexpensive medication could hold an unexpected clue to preventing dementia. Researchers found that older adults with a specific genetic profile had a 70% lower relative risk of dementia when taking low-dose aspirin, even though previous studies found no overall protective effect. The discovery suggests that genetics could help explain why some people benefit while others do not.

articles.summary: arXiv:2610.35942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: I consider what it means for AI assistance to save time. articles.title: The autistic brain processes faces differently than scientists thought
articles.summary: A major new study reveals that autistic children’s brains process faces differently, and those differences may begin earlier than scientists previously thought. Researchers found that brain signals associated with recognizing faces become more specialized as neurotypical children grow older, but show much less change in autistic children. The discovery could help explain why some autistic people have difficulty recognizing faces and reading emotions.
